byte_identity.note: shared-cache protocol: arm (a) made every live call and warmed the result cache; arm (b) had to hit the same keys (zero new calls checked) and reproduce every artifact byte-for-byte.  Cache keys are sha256 over the exact input the prompt is built from, so zero misses imply identical prompts; the byte-identity property is therefore exact on any backend, not a claim about model determinism.

GPTCache integration is out of scope this pass; no external-cache head-to-head is claimed.

The result cache cannot thrash within a run: max_size 100,000 exceeds the distinct-key count and ttl 3,600 s exceeds the run duration, so hit/miss decisions are a pure function of the draw sequence (computed without any backend and checked against both arms).
Mock-mode wall accounting charges the paper's constant 80 ms per simulated call; real-mode wall is measured.  No wall-clock value enters mock-mode output, which is byte-reproducible run to run.

Instruction-execution savings come from compilation and hot-path adoption (measured per arm); model-call savings come from the result cache (measured on arm (a) and priced per mode).  The two attributions are reported separately.
